Name: General function definition
Basic relationship:
f: A (Domain, definitionsmängd) -> B (Range, Värdemängd) is a rule that to every x in A yields one function value f(x) in B
Function graph/Funktionsgraf/Funktionskurva: {point(x, y): y=f(x)}
Domain D_f (set, allowed x values) -> Range V_f (set, based on allowed domain values)
Algebraic form of function: f(x) = <rule> <bound>, function contains expression and bound (as domain D_f), to every x in domain map to one y in range.
(<bound> can be omitted, and implicitly defined as the largest possible set of real numbers) e.g. f(x)=1/sqrt(x), <bound> infers to x>=0
Continous: The function is continuous for all x in the domain.

Name: Injective function (one-to-one mapping function)/Injektiv funktion
Basic relationship:
One to one mapping function, (x_1, x_2 in D_x)
f: A->B
\\A x_1!=x_2 -> f(x_1) != f(x_2) or f(x_1)=f(x_2) -> x_1=x_2

Name: Surjective function/Surjektiv funktion
Basic relationship: f: A->B, \\A y in B \\E x in A -> f(x)=y

Name: Strictly monotone function/Strängt monotona funktioner
Basic relationship:
Strictly increasing and strictly decreasing functions
f injective <=> f strictly monotone

Name: Inverse function
Basic relationship:
Bijective function, f: A->B, f^(-1): B->A, f (D_(f^(-1)) = V_f, V_(f^(-1)) = D_f)
f^(-1)(y)=x -> y=f(x), f^(-1)(f(x)) = x, f(f^(-1)(y))=y
For every y in V_f gives x in D_f -> f^(-1) inverse to f
Geometrical interpretation: mirroring in y=x

Name: Polynomial function
Number of roots
Basic relationship:
Every polynomial eqn f(x) = 0 has n roots x_1, ..., x_n, if k equal roots are counted k times
Each difference (x - x_1) is a factor of f(x):
f(x) = 0 = (x - x_1)(x - x_2)...(x - x_n)

Name: Number of real roots (Descartes Rule of Signs)
Basic relationship:
Number of positive roots = number of sign variations of f(x) or less than that by an even integer
Number of negative roots = number of sign variations of f(-x) or less than that by an even integer
Presetted values:
f(x) = x^3 + x^2 + 2*x + 2 = 0
f(x) sign changes = 0
=> # of positive roots = 0

f(-x) = -x^3 + x^2 - 2*x + 2 = 0
f(-x) sign changes = 3
=> # of negative roots = 3 or 1

Name: Number of complex roots
Basic relationship: Real coefficients -> Complex roots always occur in conjugate pairs (a \pm b*i), There is never only one complex root
Presetted values:
f(x) = x^3 + x^2 + 2*x + 2 = 0
has at least 1 negative root
=> by inspection x_1 = -1
therefore f(x) = (x + 1)(x^2 + 2) = 0
=> x_2 = sqrt(2)*i, x_3 = -sqrt(2)*i

Name: Location of real roots
Basic relationship: If f(a) and f(b) are opposite signs, there are at least one or an odd number of roots between a and b
Presetted values:
f(x) = 8x^3 - 12x^2 - 2*x + 3 = 0
f(-1) = -15, f(0) = 3
f(1) = -3, f(2) = 15
therefore real root exists in each of intervals:
(-1, 0), (0, 1), (1, 2)

Name: Relationship between coefficients p_i and roots x_i
Basic relationship:
-p_1 = sum of all roots
p_2 = sum of all products of roots taken two at a time
-p_3 = sum of all products of roots taken three at a time
(-1)^n * p_n = product of all roots
